setups.shielding_gas: Gas shielded (solid core wire); determine appropriate shielding gas from the Settings Chart on the inside of the Welder door. When using C100 shielding gas, use the enclosed CGA 580/320 adapter on the Regulator inlet.
setups.note: Manual labels this 'DCEP Direct Current Electrode Positive Wire Setup for Solid Core (gas shielded) welding'; diagram reads 'Ground Clamp Cable in Negative Socket' and 'Wire Feed Power Cable in Positive Socket'. Twist cables clockwise all the way to lock in place. Quick start adds: connect MIG gun to wire feed and connect wire feed control inside welder.

Manual labels this 'DCEN Direct Current Electrode Negative Wire Setup for Flux-Cored (gasless) welding'; diagram reads 'Ground Clamp Cable in Positive Socket' and 'Wire Feed Power Cable in Negative Socket'. Twist cables clockwise all the way to lock in place. Quick start: follow MIG cable setup but reverse ground clamp and wire feed power terminals.

setups.shielding_gas: Gas line connected to gas regulator (gas type not specified in these sources)
setups.note: Quick start guide TIG cable setup: ground clamp to positive terminal, TIG torch to negative terminal, gas line to gas regulator, foot pedal connected inside welder, wire feed power left disconnected. Polarity designation follows the manual's definition of DCEN as electrode negative; the sources do not print 'DCEN' for TIG.

Stick Setup diagram reads 'Ground Clamp Cable in Negative Socket' and 'Electrode Holder Cable in Positive Socket'; twist clockwise all the way to lock in place. The Stick Welding polarity screen shows ground clamp on '–', electrode on '+', and 'No Gas Required'. Quick start also says to leave wire feed power disconnected. Polarity designation follows the manual's definition of electrode positive; the sources do not print 'DCEP' for Stick.

problems.problem: Wire Feed Motor Runs but Wire Does Not Feed Properly

causes.cause: Insufficient wire feed pressure.
causes.solution: Increase wire feed pressure properly. Follow step 27 on page 17.

causes.cause: Incorrect wire feed roller size.
causes.solution: Flip roll to correct size. Follow the Feed Roller instructions on page 12.

causes.cause: Damaged MIG Gun, cable, or liner assembly.
causes.solution: Have a qualified technician inspect these parts and replace as necessary.

causes.cause: Feed Tensioner is too tight.
causes.solution: Loosen Feed Tensioner so it applies only enough pressure to prevent continued spinning after the Gun Trigger is released.

problems.problem: Wire Creates a Bird's Nest During Operation

causes.cause: Excess wire feed pressure.
causes.solution: Adjust wire feed pressure properly. Follow step 27 on page 17.

causes.cause: Incorrect Contact Tip size.
causes.solution: Replace with the proper tip for wire used.

causes.cause: MIG Gun Cable Connector not fully inserted into Wire Feed mechanism.
causes.solution: Insert Gun Cable Connector properly. Follow steps 13 and 14 on page 13.

causes.cause: Damaged liner.
causes.solution: Have a qualified technician inspect and repair/replace as necessary.

causes.cause: Gun cable is severely bent and Wire Feed mechanism cannot feed wire.
causes.solution: Straighten Gun cable.

causes.cause: Gun liner is clogged or worn.
causes.solution: Check gun liner for obstruction. Replace if necessary.

causes.cause: Gun liner is too small for welding wire being used.
causes.solution: Check that gun liner is correct size for wire.

causes.cause: Wire is tangled on the spool.
causes.solution: Check wire for cross winding or tangled spool.

causes.cause: Wire is not making contact with Feed Rollers.
causes.solution: Check Feed Rollers and ensure correct groove for wire diameter is being used.

causes.cause: Feed Roller is not making enough contact with wire or is crushing flux-cored wire.
causes.solution: Check Feed Tensioner and ensure it is set properly.

causes.cause: Wire not feeding properly.
causes.solution: See first Troubleshooting section above.

causes.cause: Incorrect Contact Tip or liner size or excessive wear.
causes.solution: Replace with the proper tip or liner size for wire used.

causes.cause: Incorrect wire feed speed.
causes.solution: Adjust wire feed speed to achieve a more stable arc.

causes.cause: Loose MIG Gun cable or ground cable.
causes.solution: Check to ensure that all connections are tight.

causes.cause: Damaged MIG Gun or loose connection within Gun.
causes.solution: Have a qualified technician inspect and repair/replace as necessary.

causes.cause: Incorrect polarity for process being run.
causes.solution: Ensure polarity is correct for operation: DCEP for MIG welding and DCEN for Flux-Cored self-shielded welding.

causes.cause: Gas coverage may be insufficient or too high.
causes.solution: Ensure gas flow rate is set according to Settings Chart. Make sure MIG Gun Cable Connector is fully inserted into Wire Feed mechanism with no O-Rings exposed.

causes.cause: Poor connection with workpiece.
causes.solution: Check the ground clamp connection to the workpiece and machine. Ensure the MIG Gun is properly secured.

causes.cause: Incorrect line voltage.
causes.solution: Check the line voltage and, if insufficient, have a licensed electrician remedy the situation.

causes.cause: Improper gauge or length of cord.
causes.solution: Do not use an extension cord on this Welder. Use only one of the supplied power cords for this Welder or an identical replacement cord.

causes.cause: Not enough current.
causes.solution: Switch current to proper setting for metal thickness.

problems.problem: Welder Does Not Function When Switched On

causes.cause: Tripped thermal protection device.
causes.solution: If a warning screen appears in the LCD Display window, Welder may have overheated and shut down. Stop and wait with the Power Switch ON for the Welder to cool. The Welder automatically returns to service after cooling off. Reduce duration or frequency of welding periods to help reduce wear on the Welder. Refer to Duty Cycle (Duration of Use) on page 19.

causes.cause: Circuit supplies insufficient input voltage or amperage.
causes.solution: Verify that the circuit is designed to supply the required input voltage and amperage as detailed on the Specifications table. If a warning screen appears in the LCD Display window, check the input voltage to ensure it is within specified range.

causes.cause: Faulty or improperly connected Trigger.
causes.solution: Ensure the gun connection is properly seated on machine. Qualified technician must check and secure/replace Trigger.

causes.cause: Machine is in low- or over-voltage protection.
causes.solution: Check input voltage and ensure it falls within the specified range. If input voltage is correct, press Reset Button on back of machine.

causes.cause: Machine is in the incorrect mode.
causes.solution: Ensure the correct process has been selected.

problems.problem: LCD Display Does Not Light When Welder is Switched On

causes.cause: Unit is not connected to outlet properly.
causes.solution: Verify the voltage at the outlet and the connection to the outlet.

causes.cause: Outlet is unpowered.
causes.solution: Check circuit breaker/GFCI devices; if any are tripped, determine and remedy cause before resetting.

causes.cause: Plug does not have correct rating.
causes.solution: Make sure installed plug is correct rating. See Specifications on page 7.

causes.cause: Circuit breaker has tripped due to high input amperage.
causes.solution: Press Reset Button on back of machine to reset circuit breaker.

causes.cause: Input Power Cord is not seated properly.
causes.solution: Ensure the twist lock input Power Cord is fully secured.

problems.problem: Wire Feeds, but Arc Does Not Ignite

causes.cause: Improper ground connection.
causes.solution: Make certain that the workpiece is contacted properly by the Ground Clamp and that the workpiece is properly cleaned near the ground clamp and the welding location.

causes.cause: Improperly sized Contact Tip.
causes.solution: Verify that Contact Tip is the proper size for welding wire. If needed, replace Contact Tip with proper size and type.

causes.cause: Excessively worn Contact Tip.
causes.solution: Check that the hole in the tip is not deformed or enlarged. If needed, replace Contact Tip with proper size and type.

causes.cause: Dirty Contact Tip.
causes.solution: Properly clean Contact Tip.

causes.cause: Shielding gas bottle is empty.
causes.solution: Check gas bottle and replenish as necessary.

causes.cause: Not enough or too much shielding gas.
causes.solution: Check gas regulator to ensure proper flow.

causes.cause: Dirty workpiece.
causes.solution: Clean workpiece down to bare metal.

causes.cause: Gun is being used too far away from workpiece.
causes.solution: Check CTWD (contact tip to work distance) for the proper procedure.

causes.cause: Polarity is incorrect for the application.
causes.solution: Check the polarity and ensure it is DCEP for MIG and DCEN for Flux-Cored.

causes.cause: Dirty welding wire is introducing contamination into the weld.
causes.solution: Make certain that welding wire is clean and free of rust and residues.

problems.problem: Welder Does Not Function When Switched On

causes.cause: Tripped thermal protection device.
causes.solution: Reduce duration or frequency of welding periods to help reduce wear on the welder. Refer to Duty Cycle (Duration of Use) on page 29.

causes.cause: Faulty or improperly connected Trigger.
causes.solution: Qualified technician must check and secure/replace Trigger.

causes.cause: Ground Clamp not attached to workpiece.
causes.solution: Attach Ground Clamp to workpiece.

causes.cause: Shielding Gas not connected.
causes.solution: Connect shielding gas to Welder.

problems.problem: LCD Display Does Not Light When Welder is Switched On

causes.cause: Unit is not connected to outlet properly.
causes.solution: Verify the voltage at the outlet and the connection to the outlet.

causes.cause: Outlet is unpowered.
causes.solution: Check circuit breaker/GFCI devices; if any are tripped, determine and remedy cause before resetting. Verify that the circuit is designed to supply the required input amperage as detailed in Specifications on page 7.

causes.cause: Incorrect line voltage.
causes.solution: Check the line voltage and, if insufficient, have a licensed electrician remedy the situation.

causes.cause: Improper gauge or length of cord.
causes.solution: Do not use an extension cord on this Welder. Use only one of the supplied power cords for this Welder or an identical replacement cord.

causes.cause: Loose electrode cable or ground cable.
causes.solution: Check to ensure that all connections are tight.

causes.cause: Damaged electrode holder or loose connection within electrode holder.
causes.solution: Have a qualified technician inspect and repair/replace as necessary.

causes.cause: Adjust current setting.
causes.solution: Make sure setting matches recommended setting on chart.

causes.cause: Shielding gas getting low.
causes.solution: Replace shielding gas cylinder.

steps.title: Connect gun cable to wire feed
steps.detail: Loosen the Knob on the Wire Feed mechanism, pass the Gun Cable Connector through the hole in the Welder front and into the socket, seat it fully, then tighten the Knob securely. If the Connector is not fully inserted the gas connection will leak and shielding gas will not reach the arc; do not overtighten the Knob.

steps.title: Connect wire feed control cable
steps.detail: Insert the Wire Feed Control Cable through the hole in the Welder front and connect it to the Wire Feed Control Socket inside the machine, then tighten the lock ring. The plug fits the socket in one orientation only.

steps.title: Set DCEP polarity for solid core wire
steps.detail: Plug the Ground Clamp Cable into the Negative (-) Socket and the Wire Feed Power Cable into the Positive (+) Socket. Twist both cables clockwise all the way to lock them in place.

steps.title: Select and secure shielding gas cylinder
steps.detail: Decide which shielding gas suits your work using the Settings Chart on the inside of the Welder door. With assistance, set the cylinder (not included) on a cabinet or cart near the Welder and secure it with two straps (not included) to prevent tipping.

steps.title: Purge the cylinder valve
steps.detail: Remove the cylinder's cap, stand to the side of the valve opening, and open the valve briefly to blow dust and dirt out. Close the cylinder valve.

steps.title: Fit regulator and gas hose
steps.detail: Close the Regulator valve until it is loose, thread the Regulator onto the cylinder and wrench-tighten. When using C100 gas, wrench-tighten the enclosed CGA 580/320 adapter between Regulator inlet and cylinder. Attach the Gas Hose to the Regulator outlet and the Welder's gas inlet and wrench-tighten both connections.

steps.title: Prepare and clamp the workpieces
steps.detail: Clean the weld surfaces to bare metal with a wire brush or angle grinder, with no rust, paint or oil left. Hold the pieces with clamps at a controlled gap, chamfering the edges of thicker workpieces for full penetration, and make practice welds on scrap of the same thickness first.

steps.title: Attach ground clamp to bare metal
steps.detail: Clamp the Ground Cable to bare metal on the workpiece near the weld area, or to the metal work bench holding the workpiece. When welding equipment on a vehicle, disconnect the battery from both the positive connection and the ground first.

steps.title: Connect power and switch on
steps.detail: With the Power Switch OFF, plug the Power Cord into a properly grounded, GFCI protected 120VAC (20 amp rated) or 240VAC receptacle that matches the plug and is protected by a delayed action-type breaker or fuses. Set the MIG Gun on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface away from grounded objects, then turn the Power Switch ON.

steps.title: Select the MIG process
steps.detail: Press the Home Button on the Control Panel, turn the Main Control Knob until the desired process appears on the LCD screen, then press the Main Control Knob to select it. The Back Button returns to the previous screen.

steps.title: Confirm polarity and gas screen
steps.detail: Plug the cables in and connect the gas as shown on the polarity and gas screen, then set the flow between 20-30 SCFH.

steps.title: Set wire size, thickness and weld values
steps.detail: Turn the Left Knob for wire diameter and the Right Knob for material thickness, then on the Auto Weld screen turn the Left Knob for Wire Feed Speed (Amperage) and the Right Knob for Voltage. If adjusted manually, the white mark on the line shows the recommended setting for your wire diameter and workpiece thickness.

steps.title: Connect gun cable to wire feed
steps.detail: Loosen the Knob on the Wire Feed mechanism, push the Gun Cable Connector through the hole in the Welder front and fully into the socket, then tighten the Knob securely without overtightening.

steps.title: Connect wire feed control cable
steps.detail: Run the Wire Feed Control Cable through the hole in the Welder front, plug it into the Wire Feed Control Socket inside the machine in its one correct orientation, and tighten the lock ring on the plug.

steps.title: Set DCEN polarity for gasless wire
steps.detail: Plug the Ground Clamp Cable into the Positive (+) Socket and the Wire Feed Power Cable into the Negative (-) Socket. Twist both cables clockwise all the way to lock in place.

steps.title: Prepare and clamp the workpieces
steps.detail: Clean the weld surfaces down to bare metal so no rust, paint or oil remains, and clamp the pieces with a controlled gap, chamfering thick edges for penetration. Practice on scrap of the same thickness before welding anything of value.

steps.title: Attach ground clamp to bare metal
steps.detail: Clamp the Ground Cable to bare metal on the workpiece near the weld, or to the metal bench the workpiece is clamped to. On vehicles, disconnect the battery from both the positive connection and the ground before welding.

steps.title: Plug in the power cord
steps.detail: With the Power Switch OFF, plug the Power Cord into a properly grounded, GFCI protected 120VAC (20 amp rated) or 240VAC receptacle matching the plug, on a circuit with delayed action-type breaker or fuses.

steps.title: Rest the gun and switch on
steps.detail: Set the MIG Gun down on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface away from any grounded objects, then turn the Power Switch ON.

steps.title: Select the process on screen
steps.detail: Press the Home Button, turn the Main Control Knob until the desired process appears on the LCD display, then press the Main Control Knob to select it.

steps.title: Follow the polarity screen
steps.detail: Plug the cables in according to the polarity screen shown for the selected process, and connect gas according to the screen if the screen calls for it.

steps.title: Set wire diameter and thickness
steps.detail: Turn the Left Knob to set the wire diameter and the Right Knob to set the material thickness, then press the Main Control Knob to continue.

steps.title: Set wire feed speed and voltage
steps.detail: On the Auto Weld screen turn the Left Knob to adjust Wire Feed Speed (Amperage) and the Right Knob to adjust Voltage. If set manually, the white mark on the line shows the recommended setting for your wire diameter and workpiece thickness.

steps.title: Assemble the TIG torch
steps.detail: Consult the Settings Chart on top of the Welder for the correct Tungsten Electrode size for your material, match Collet and Collet Body to that size, thread the Collet Body into the front of the Torch and the Ceramic Nozzle onto the Collet Body. Insert the Collet from the back into the Collet Body, insert the Electrode from the front, and lock it with the Back Cap so it protrudes 1/8" to 1/4" beyond the Ceramic Nozzle.

steps.title: Sharpen the tungsten electrode
steps.detail: Shut off the welder and let the Electrode and Torch cool, remove the Back Cap and pull the Electrode out the front, snapping off any contaminated end with pliers. Grind lightly on a dedicated fine grit wheel, rotating the tip and grinding parallel to the Electrode length until a blunt point about 2-1/2 times the Electrode diameter in length is formed, then reinstall it protruding 1/8"-1/4" beyond the Ceramic Nozzle.
steps.warning: WARNING! TO PREVENT SERIOUS INJURY: Some Electrodes may have materials added to them that are hazardous to breathe. Wear a respirator and ANSI-approved Safety goggles when grinding an Electrode.

steps.title: Secure the argon cylinder
steps.detail: With assistance, place a 100% Argon cylinder (not included) onto a cabinet or cart near the Welder and secure it with two straps (not included) to prevent tipping.

steps.title: Purge valve and fit regulator
steps.detail: Remove the cylinder's cap, stand to the side of the valve opening and open the valve briefly to blow out dust and dirt, then close it. Close the Regulator valve until loose, thread the Regulator onto the cylinder and wrench-tighten the connection.

steps.title: Connect the shielding gas hose
steps.detail: Connect the Shielding Gas Hose on the TIG Torch Cable Connector to the Regulator's outlet and wrench-tighten the connection.

steps.title: Plug cord into power input socket
steps.detail: Plug either the 120VAC or 240VAC Power Cord into the Power Input Socket on the Welder; the plug will only fit one way.
steps.warning: WARNING! TO PREVENT SERIOUS INJURY FROM ACCIDENTAL OPERATION: Do not plug cord into wall outlet at this time.

steps.title: Open gas and set flow
steps.detail: Open the gas cylinder's valve all the way, then set the Flow Gauge to the SCFH value shown on the Settings Chart inside the Welder door.
steps.warning: DANGER - TO PREVENT DEATH FROM ASPHYXIATION: Do not open gas without proper ventilation. Fix gas leaks immediately. Shielding gas can displace air and cause rapid loss of consciousness and death. Shielding gas without carbon dioxide can be even more hazardous because asphyxiation can start without feeling shortness of breath.

steps.title: Plug welder into the outlet
steps.detail: With the Power Switch OFF, plug the Welder into a properly grounded, GFCI protected 120VAC (20 amp rated) outlet or 240V outlet on a circuit with delayed action-type circuit breaker or fuses.

steps.title: Rest the torch and power on
steps.detail: Set the TIG Torch down on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface away from any grounded objects, then turn the Power Switch ON.
steps.warning: WARNING - TO PREVENT SERIOUS INJURY AND DEATH: Do not weld without Grounding Clamp. When the operator is not holding the Torch, it must be sitting on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface. Only hold TIG Rod with an electrically insulated welding glove.

steps.title: Select the TIG process
steps.detail: Press the Home Button on the Control Panel, turn the Main Control Knob until the TIG process appears on the LCD display, then press the Main Control Knob to select it. The Back Button returns to the previous screen.

steps.title: Confirm polarity and gas screen
steps.detail: Plug the cables in and connect the gas according to the screen shown, then set the flow between 10-25 SCFH.

steps.title: Set rod size, thickness and amperage
steps.detail: Turn the Left Knob for rod diameter and the Right Knob for material thickness, then on the Auto Weld screen turn the Left Knob to adjust output amperage and the Right Knob to ON to energize the TIG Torch.
steps.warning: WARNING! TO PREVENT SERIOUS INJURY: Welder is now energized and Open Circuit Voltage is present.

steps.title: Connect the ground clamp cable
steps.detail: Plug the Ground Clamp Cable into the Negative Socket and twist it clockwise all the way to lock it in place.

steps.title: Connect the electrode holder cable
steps.detail: Plug the Electrode Holder Cable into the Positive Socket and twist it clockwise all the way to lock it in place.

steps.title: Plug cord into power input socket
steps.detail: Plug either the 120VAC or 240VAC Power Cord into the Power Input Socket; the plug will only fit one way.
steps.warning: WARNING! TO PREVENT SERIOUS INJURY FROM ACCIDENTAL OPERATION: Do not plug cord into wall outlet at this time.

steps.title: Plug welder into the outlet
steps.detail: Turn the Power Switch to the OFF position, then plug the Welder into a properly grounded, GFCI protected 120VAC (20 amp rated) outlet or 240V outlet on a circuit with delayed action-type circuit breaker or fuses.

steps.title: Rest the electrode holder safely
steps.detail: Set the Electrode Holder down on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface away from any grounded objects.
steps.warning: WARNING - TO PREVENT SERIOUS INJURY AND DEATH: Do not weld without Grounding Clamp. When the operator is not holding the Electrode Holder, it must be sitting on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface.

steps.title: Turn the power switch on
steps.detail: Switch the Welder's Power Switch to the ON position.

steps.title: Select the STICK process
steps.detail: Press the Home Button on the Control Panel, turn the Main Control Knob until the Stick process appears on the LCD display, then press the Main Control Knob to select STICK. The Back Button returns to the previous screen.

steps.title: Follow the polarity screen
steps.detail: Plug the cables in according to the polarity screen shown for the Stick process; the screen indicates no gas is required.

steps.title: Set the electrode type
steps.detail: Turn the Main Control Knob to set the electrode type on the Stick electrode screen.

steps.title: Set electrode diameter and thickness
steps.detail: Turn the Left Knob to set the electrode diameter and the Right Knob to set the material thickness.

steps.title: Set amperage and energize holder
steps.detail: On the Auto Weld screen, turn the Left Knob to adjust output amperage, then turn the Right Knob to ON to energize the Electrode Holder.
steps.warning: WARNING! TO PREVENT SERIOUS INJURY: Welder is now energized and Open Circuit Voltage is present.
